story_type: disabled gambling ship in heavy seas, basket hoist
hook: A gambling ship lost power 17 miles out, in heavy seas
narration: This gambling ship lost power seventeen miles off Florida, in heavy seas.
Another boat took it in tow, but the line parted during the night.
The next day, a Coast Guard helicopter from Savannah came for the five men aboard.
The flight mechanic runs the hoist and talks the pilot into place, because the pilot can't see below.
One by one, they rode the basket up off the rolling deck.
outcome: The Savannah helicopter crew rescued all five men from the Sun Cruz 9.
title: Gambling ship adrift in heavy seas
description:
On March 8, 2008, a Coast Guard helicopter crew from Air Station Savannah rescued five men from the disabled gambling ship Sun Cruz 9, 17 miles off St. Augustine, Florida, after its tow line parted in heavy seas.

Footage: Coast Guard video by Lt. James Willingham, Air Station Savannah, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/313217/3-8-08-sun-cruz-9-rescue

facts.claim: Savannah helicopter crew rescued five men from disabled gambling ship 17 miles off St. Augustine
facts.source_quote: A helicopter crew from Air Station Savannah, Ga., rescue five men from the disabled gambling ship Sun Cruz 9 17-miles off the coast of St. Augustine, Fla., March 8, 2008.
The gambling ship left Fort Lauderdale, Fla., for Jacksonville to make repairs when it lost power.

facts.claim: Tow line parted in heavy seas at night
facts.source_quote: The ship then hired another vessel to tow it the rest of the way when the line parted in heavy seas during the night of March 7, 2008.
